scenarios.name: User Registration and Authentication Flow
scenarios.reason: Tracing shows RegisterAsync hashes password and stores user with 'User' role. AuthenticateAsync correctly verifies hash. Seeded admin user 'admin@certeasy.local' with password 'Admin@123' is correctly configured in DbContext.
evidence: AccountService.RegisterAsync uses IPasswordService to hash and save.
CertEasyDbContext seeds Admin user with pre-calculated hash 'AQAAAAEAACcQAAAAEPvR3zU+YyW6n6Uf8n3H6J6V6L6X6n6X6n6X6n6X6n6X6n6X6n6X6n6X6n6X6n6X6n6X6n=='.
fixes_applied: Updated CertEasyDbContext.cs to use a valid PasswordHasher-generated hash for the seeded admin user.

scenarios.name: Windows Authentication and Auto-registration
scenarios.reason: AccountController.WindowsLogin triggers Negotiate challenge. AccountService.GetUserByWindowsIdentityAsync handles user lookup or auto-creation for Windows identities.
evidence: AccountService handles Windows user creation if missing.

scenarios.name: Multi-step Certification Application Wizard
scenarios.reason: Wizard UI (Apply.cshtml) using Knockout.js correctly maps to WorkflowController. SubmitApplication performs server-side validation against duplicate pending applications.
evidence: WorkflowService.SubmitApplicationAsync checks for existing pending apps for the same certification/user.

scenarios.name: Admin Review and Master Data Management
scenarios.reason: AdminController allows approval/rejection of applications. AdminService updates status and logs actions using Serilog. ManageCertifications and ManageEducation provide CRUD-like status toggling.
evidence: AdminService.ApproveApplicationAsync sets status to Approved and logs to 'AppLogs'.
AdminController.Index filters for applications in 'Review' status.

scenarios.name: Database Persistence and Schema Safety
scenarios.reason: Program.cs runs dbContext.Database.Migrate() at startup. DbContext configures NoAction for Application-User FK to prevent cascade cycles. Logs table collision is avoided by mapping Log entity to 'AppLogs'.
evidence: Program.cs contains migration execution logic in service scope.
